affects.title: What affects cost
affects.subtitle: Three factors shape what your plan should look like.

volume.title: Data volume
volume.body: The biggest single driver — how much data moves per job and per month.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.body: One-time migrations, recurring backups, and continuous sync each price differently.

runner.title: Where the transfer runs
runner.body: If we host it, you pay for the bandwidth we use. If it runs in your browser tab or on your own server, you don't.

cloudVsPrivate.title: Where the bytes flow changes the cost.
cloudVsPrivate.subtitle: Same orchestration, different data path. Pick what fits your trust and volume.

cloud.title: On our servers
cloud.scenario: Files travel through our infrastructure. We handle the bandwidth, retries, and isolation. You pay per transfer — cost rises as you move more data.
cloud.bestFor: you want convenience, scheduled jobs, and migrations you don't have to babysit.

private.title: On your own server
private.scenario: Files travel through your server, NAS, or VPS. We only orchestrate the job — you bring the bandwidth. Pay a flat monthly fee, regardless of volume.
private.bestFor: you care about privacy, run a homelab, or move high volumes on your own bandwidth.

earlyAccess.headline: Join now, lock in early access.
earlyAccess.body: Nobody pays yet. Waitlist members get the first invitations at launch.

items.a: The four-plan structure is set. Exact prices may shift at the margins before launch — that's why each tier shows a `~` instead of an exact number.

items.q: Will there be an annual plan with a discount?
items.a: Yes — we plan to offer an annual option at a discount, but the exact pricing isn't set. It will most likely launch alongside the paid plans, not before.

items.q: What if I move more data than my plan includes?
items.a: Free includes 5 GB/month on our servers with no paid overage — once you hit the cap, your browser tab is the only hosted option that month. Pro and Business add 1 TB for $2.50 each time you go over. Private Runner has no GB cap; you pay a flat fee and bring your own bandwidth.

items.q: Do Browser Runner and Private Runner count against my GB allowance?
items.a: No. Only the Cloud Runner uses our hosted bandwidth, so only the Cloud Runner counts against your monthly GB. Browser Runner runs in your browser tab and Private Runner runs on your own server — files never touch our infrastructure, so neither consumes your allowance.
We plan a path toward source-visible, self-hostable infrastructure. Pricing for that path will be set when the model itself is set — see the self-hosted page for details.

items.q: Will I be charged automatically when launch happens?
items.a: No. Joining the waitlist never bills you. Anyone moving from waitlist to a paid plan does so explicitly.

items.q: What happens if my use case spans two plans?
items.a: Pick the closer one and tell us in the waitlist questions. We'll reach out before launch if a different plan fits better.

developers.title: Developers — automate cloud file transfers
developers.description: Move files between clouds with a typed HTTP API, a CLI, webhooks, and runners you can host yourself.
developers.heroHeadline: Move files between clouds with one API.
developers.heroSubheading: For agencies, SaaS teams, and internal tools that move files between cloud providers without writing the glue.
developers.audienceLabel: Built for agencies, SaaS engineering teams, platform groups, and internal tooling.
developers.apiBody: Create a job with a source, destination, runner, and optional schedule. The control plane validates, dispatches, and emits progress events.
developers.apiCaption: Sketch — final shape will land with the v1 API.
developers.oauthBody: Your users connect their cloud accounts to Syncologic, not to your app. You never store provider credentials. The control plane manages the OAuth lifecycle and hands out scoped, short-lived tokens to runners — your app authenticates with Syncologic via your API key and never sees a provider token.
developers.oauthCaption: Your app integrates the API; the OAuth boundary stays on our side.
developers.cliTitle: A CLI for scripts and CI
developers.cliBody: Same jobs, driven from a terminal or a CI runner. Useful for one-shot migrations and for backups owned by a script you can read in a code review.
developers.cliCaption: Planned. Behavior mirrors the API one-to-one.
developers.runnersTitle: Pick the runner that fits the job
developers.runnersBody: Same API. Three different data paths. Choose per job, not per account.
developers.runnersFooterText: Want the full Private Runner walkthrough?

runnerCloud.title: Cloud Runner
runnerCloud.desc: Hosted runners for scheduled jobs and large migrations. No infrastructure on your side.

runnerBrowser.title: Browser Runner
runnerBrowser.desc: For ad-hoc transfers from a tab. The data path stays in the user's browser; no long-lived tokens.

runnerPrivate.title: Private Runner
runnerPrivate.desc: Self-host the runner binary on a VPS, on-prem server, or NAS. Outbound-only connection to the control plane.

developers.webhooksTitle: Webhooks for the events you care about
developers.webhooksBody: Subscribe to job lifecycle events and stream them into your queue, your dashboard, or your audit log. Payloads will be HMAC-signed.
developers.noSdkBody: We will not ship an official SDK before the API is stable. The OpenAPI spec will be public, so you can generate a typed client in any language you already use.

faq.a: We're not committing to a date. The API ships with the first paid Cloud Runner tier — join the waitlist for early access.

faq.q: Will there be a free tier for developers?
faq.a: There's no special developer offer — everything you'd pay (or not pay) is in the current plans.

faq.q: Do you handle OAuth on behalf of my users?
faq.a: Yes — your app never holds a provider token.

faq.q: Can I run jobs entirely on my own infrastructure?
faq.a: Yes for the data path — Private Runner runs on any server you control, and file bytes never reach Syncologic.
Webhook payloads will be HMAC-signed with a per-workspace secret you control.

meta.title: Run transfers on your own server — Syncologic
meta.description: Move files between clouds with the data path running entirely on your own server, NAS, or VPS. Files never pass through our infrastructure.

hero.headline: Run everything on your own server.
hero.subheading: Files never pass through our infrastructure. You install a small program, connect your clouds to it, and the transfer runs inside your network.
hero.audience: For homelab operators, privacy-conscious users, and businesses that want their file transfers running on infrastructure they control.

howItWorks.title: How it works for you
howItWorks.intro: You run the transfer on your own server. We coordinate the job; the bytes never reach us. We call this setup a Private Runner.

filesStay.title: Files never park on our servers
filesStay.desc: Bytes travel from the source cloud, through your server, to the destination cloud. Our infrastructure never sees the files.

credentials.title: Your credentials stay with you
credentials.desc: Provider tokens live where your runner runs. We never receive them.

noInbound.title: No incoming connections to open
noInbound.desc: Your server reaches out to us. No firewall holes, no exposed services, no port-forwarding.

underTheHood.summary: How it works under the hood
underTheHood.intro: Architecture, the self-host roadmap, and why core code stays public — for the technical buyer.

controlData.title: Control plane vs data plane
controlData.body: Two layers. The control plane (auth, jobs, schedules, reports) holds metadata about your transfers. The data plane (the runner) is where bytes flow source → destination. We host the control plane at launch; you host the data plane from day one.

roadmap.title: Self-host levels

level1.name: Private Runner
level1.desc: Hosted control plane, your data path. For users who want our convenience and your bandwidth.

level2.name: Full self-host
level2.desc: Bring your own control plane. Your auth, your database, your runners. Same product, your infrastructure.

roadmap.footnote: Plus an air-gapped variant for high-compliance environments that can't reach the public internet.

sourceVisible.title: Why core code stays public
sourceVisible.body: Runner code, transfer logic, and provider adapters ship source-visible. You can audit how files move before trusting the system.
